answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% spend cut and the incumbent has refused to reprice. The contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so staying put forces a renegotiation that the incumbent has already declined; renewing on current terms fails the mandate. memory_c6 (multi-year commitments with incumbent) is a weaker lever here because the incumbent has closed the door on price this cycle, and a long-term commitment does not address the immediate cost gap. The low-cost vendor's quote meets the mandate on its own, so a primary switch is the cleanest path. memory_c2 supports this direction: that vendor cut unit cost sharply last year, onboarded quickly, and invoiced accurately, so total cost of ownership should improve without integration-driven delivery risk. Operating at 94% of committed volume with no buffer keeps this a broad rollout risk, so preservation notes flag the validation gaps (current quality performance, continuity through the 14-day transition) and the decision could still be revisited if verification surfaces new information.
